backend.title: Backend in practice: ServiceOS
backend.intro: ServiceOS is a multi-tenant SaaS with an AI receptionist for online booking, built by our team and still in early development. This is the architecture it follows, and how I think about backends in general.

layers.d: React components never call a provider SDK directly.
Business logic lives in server-only services. Input is validated with zod.
Repository, auth and AI contracts that belong to us, not to a vendor.
Today a local and an in-memory adapter, a Supabase adapter planned. Swapping a provider costs one adapter, not a rewrite.

notes: Audited: no provider SDK in the core

beauty.summary: A booking-focused website for a lash, nail and hair studio, built as a template: every colour, size, text, photo and contact detail lives in one config, so the next client is a day of work instead of a rebuild.
points: Design tokens as the single source of truth: palette, type scale, spacing and motion timings in one file. Changing the primitives restyles the whole site.
Motion with intent: GSAP and Lenis, split-text reveals, a liquid chrome WebGL shape, depth sections such as tunnel, doors and card decks, a magnifier lens and a text scramble on hover.
Booking without a backend: a step-by-step wizard (service, first and backup day, time of day, name) that prepares a WhatsApp message. Nothing is stored or sent to a server.
Three languages and real SEO: DE, UK and EN with next-intl, sitemap, manifest, structured data, security headers and a strict content security policy.

noform.summary: A cinematic brand site for a fictional fashion label: one long scroll made of full-screen scenes, with sound, a strict mono type system and a restrained palette.
points: Scroll-driven scenes: GSAP ScrollTrigger and Observer run a sequence of full-screen scenes instead of a page of sections.
Motion studies: a lettering ring, a helix archive and a depth flight, each built as a separate experiment before it became part of the site.
A motion director that coordinates scene timing, the preloader and the sound toggle, with reduced-motion fallbacks.
Three languages (DE, EN, UK) with a typographic system that holds up in every one.

pizza.summary: A scroll storyboard for a pizza and döner delivery site: toppings lift and fall, the camera pivots, a yufka rolls in and the box opens, all on one scrubbed timeline.
points: Storyboard first: a written shot list with scroll percentages for every beat before any code.
2.5D sprite choreography: separate topping sprites on their own paths, with rotation, easing and landing spots.
Honest motion: where true 3D was not available, the sequence uses a cinematic cut instead of faking physics.
Mobile and reduced-motion variants: fewer sprites, shorter sequences and a static fallback.

hire.pitch: I am a web developer who covers the whole path of a website: design, build, deployment and SEO tracking. I do not hand work over, I carry it to a measurable result. I build fast, search-friendly, multilingual sites with motion, and I work every day with AI tools such as Claude Code and GPT, with clear rules and a check on every step. A team gets more done in less time, without losing quality. I am open to a position inside a company or to freelance work, whichever fits.

why.d: Layout, code, deployment and SEO tracking in one head. Fewer handoffs, faster decisions, one owner.
I use Claude Code and GPT every day. I write the rules and the spec, the AI does the heavy typing, and I verify every result. Fast without being sloppy.
Eight projects, three case studies, a public GitHub history and a measured Lighthouse on this very site.
Fluid layouts, accessibility, performance and multilingual support, including right-to-left, are the default, not an extra.
Small, checked steps, clear commits and an honest status. German B1, Ukrainian and Russian in conversation, English and documentation with AI tools.
